title: \(X\)-evolve: Solution space evolution powered by large language models

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-generated tunable solution-space evolution for combinatorial optimization and online bin packing
mechanism.populationDetail: The global program database accumulates valid compacted tunable programs without explicit islands or maintained genealogy; score clusters are sampling partitions. \(K_{\mathrm{search}}\) parallel processes are restarted by adaptive halving, not migration-based islands.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The database partitions top-score entries into a separate cluster for sampling, but no distinct persistent elite archive/storage separate from the accumulated database is described.
mechanism.replacementDetail: After inner X-search, the tunable program is compacted to decisions present in top-K evaluated combinations and the valid compacted program is appended with its maximum score; invalid and timeout programs are excluded. No database capacity cleanup is specified.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM synthesizes a new tunable priority function/program conditioned on multiple database references; inner search then samples combinations of its tunable decisions.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Each sampled program receives a scalar objective score; X-search attributes that score to every decision in the sampled combination and retains the maximum per decision. Invalid/timeout programs are excluded or yield no score. These decision-level scores guide later sampling.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: No true editable parent is identified. The \(K_{\mathrm{ref}}\) programs are auxiliary references; do not equate their count with the number of true parents. Inner X-search separately samples one value per tunable decision with softmax probabilities and tracks visited combinations.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The main contribution evolves a tunable program-defined Cartesian solution space, then searches and compacts its individual decision options using per-decision score attribution. This two-level representation/search mechanism is not fully captured by parent-relative offspring categories.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/X-evolve Solution space evolution powered by large language models.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The survey's Large-Scale Modification grouping appears unsupported as a direct parent-edit label: X-evolve generates a tunable function from score-selected reference implementations, without one identified editable parent. K_ref references are not confirmed true parents. The top-score cluster is a sampling partition in the same database, not a clearly separate archive. Batch evaluation is not evidence of parallel evaluator execution. Multi-model use is mostly separate-model experiments, with random per-call routing only in one ablation.
